title: The Largest Group of Strangers

concept.title: Branch on one vertex: leave it out, or take it and remove its neighbours
body: In a graph, an *independent set* is a set of vertices with **no edge between two of them** (a group of strangers). We want the largest one. Keep the set of vertices still available as a **bit mask** (bit `v` is 1 if `v` is available) and take the lowest available vertex `v`. There are two cases: `v` is **not** in the set, or `v` **is** in the set, and then `v` and all its neighbours are no longer available.

The line with `adj[v] & rest == 0` is a **reduction rule**: a vertex without available neighbours can always be taken, so no branching is needed. Without it, a graph with no edges would make the search try all `2^20` subsets. Bit masks make "remove the neighbours" a single operation, and the search stays fast for 20 vertices.

statement: A graph has `n` vertices and `m` edges. A set of vertices is *independent* if no edge joins two of them. Print the size of the largest independent set.
inputFormat: Each of the next `m` lines has two vertices joined by an edge.
constraints: 0 <= m <= n * (n - 1) / 2, no repeated edges and no loops

examples.note: A path of five vertices: the vertices 1, 3 and 5 are independent, and no set of four is.

hints: Keep the set of available vertices as a bit mask and take the lowest one.
Either skip it, or take it and remove it together with its neighbours from the mask.
If the vertex has no available neighbour, take it without branching.

explanation: The recursion takes the lowest available vertex. A vertex with no available neighbour is taken at once; otherwise the search either skips it or takes it and removes its neighbours, and keeps the larger result.
solution.complexity: Time O(1.6^n) or better with the rule, space O(n).
